en: [0] Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “‘Inopportune, inopportune,’ monks, is what the unlearned, ordinary person speaks of. Yet he does not know what is an opportune moment or what is an inopportune moment. Monks, there are these eight inopportune and unfavorable times for a person to dwell in the holy life. What are the eight?”

[1] Here, monks, a Teacher has appeared in the world: a Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. And the Dharma is taught—leading to peace, leading to final Nirvāṇa, leading to full awakening, proclaimed by the Sugata.
Yet this person is reborn in the hells; this is the first inopportune time, the unfavorable occasion for a person to dwell in the holy life.

[2] Furthermore, monks, a Teacher has appeared in the world: a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, Sugata, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. And the Dharma is taught—leading to peace, leading to final Nirvāṇa, conducive to full awakening, and proclaimed by the Sugata.
Yet this person is reborn among animals; this is the second inopportune and untimely circumstance for a person to dwell in the holy life.

[3] Furthermore, monks, a Teacher has appeared in the world: a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. And the Dharma is taught—peaceful, leading to complete nirvāṇa, conducive to full awakening, and proclaimed by the Sugata.
Yet this person is reborn among the hungry ghosts; this is the third inopportune and untimely situation for a person to dwell in the holy life.

[4] Furthermore, monks, a Teacher has appeared in the world: a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. And the Dharma is taught—peaceful, leading to complete nirvāṇa, conducive to full awakening, proclaimed by the Sugata.
Yet this person is reborn among the long-lived gods; this is the fourth inopportune and untimely occasion for a person to dwell in the holy life.

[5] Furthermore, monks, a Teacher has arisen in the world: a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. And the Dharma is taught—leading to peace, leading to final nirvana, leading to awakening, proclaimed by the Sugata.

Furthermore, this person is born in remote border regions, such as among bandits or barbarians, where there is no access for the fourfold assembly—the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—for the teaching of the Dharma. This is the fifth inopportune and unfavorable condition for a person to dwell in the holy life.

[6] Furthermore, monks, a Teacher has arisen in the world: a Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. And the Dharma is taught—leading to peace, leading to final Nirvāṇa, conducive to full awakening, proclaimed by the Sugata. And this person is born in the central regions.

And he becomes dull-witted, like a deaf-mute, communicating only by means of hand gestures, and lacks the capacity to understand the meaning of well-spoken or ill-spoken teachings. Monks, this is the sixth inopportune moment, the sixth unfavorable time for a person to dwell in the holy life.

[7] Furthermore, monks, a Teacher has appeared in the world: a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a Teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. And the Dharma is taught—leading to peace, leading to final Nirvāṇa, conducive to full awakening, proclaimed by the Sugata. And this person is born in the central regions.

And he is not dull-witted, nor is he deaf-mute, nor does he communicate by hand gestures; he is capable of understanding the meaning of teachings that are well-spoken or ill-spoken. Nevertheless, he holds wrong views, possesses perverted vision, and maintains such a view and such a doctrine.

There is no giving, no sacrifice, no oblation; there is no good conduct and no evil conduct; there is no fruition or ripening of the results of good and evil deeds; there is no this world and no other world; there is no mother and no father; there are no spontaneously born beings; and there are no Arhats in the world who have attained rightly and practiced rightly.

Those who, having realized for themselves through direct higher knowledge in this very life this world and the world beyond, and having attained and entered upon that realization, declare: "Birth is exhausted for us; the holy life has been lived; what was to be done has been accomplished; we know no further existence beyond this"—this is the seventh inopportune and unfavorable occasion for a person to dwell the holy life.

[8] Furthermore, monks, it may be that no Teacher has appeared in the world—a Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One—and likewise the Dharma is not being taught, which leads to tranquility, leads to final Nirvana, leads to perfect awakening, and has been proclaimed by the Sugata. And this person is born in the central regions.

And he is not dull-witted, nor deaf-mute, nor one who cannot speak with his hands; he is capable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken teachings. He possesses right view, seeing things without error, having such a view and speaking thus:

There is what is given, there is what is sacrificed, there is what is offered, there is good conduct, there is evil conduct; there is the fruit and ripening of deeds of good and evil conduct; there is this world, there is the other world; there is a mother, there is a father; there are spontaneously born beings; and in this world there are Arhats who have attained rightly and practiced rightly.

Those who, having realized for themselves through direct higher knowledge in this very life this world and the world beyond, having attained and fully realized it, declare: "Birth is exhausted for us; the holy life has been lived; what was to be done has been accomplished; we know no further state of existence beyond this"—this is the eighth inopportune and unfavorable time for a person to dwell the holy life.

[9] Monks, there is but one moment, one occasion, for an individual to dwell in the holy life. What, monks, is that one moment, that one occasion for an individual to dwell in the holy life? Here, monks, a Teacher has arisen in the world, a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

And the Dharma is taught—leading to tranquility, leading to final nirvana, leading to perfect enlightenment, as proclaimed by the Sugata. And this person is born in the central regions; he is not dull-witted, nor deaf-mute, nor one who cannot communicate by hand, but is capable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken teachings. He possesses right view, seeing things without error, holding such a view and speaking thus.

There is what is given, there is what is sacrificed, there is what is offered, there is good conduct, there is bad conduct; there is the fruit and ripening of deeds of good and bad conduct; there is this world, there is the other world; there is a mother, there is a father; there are spontaneously born beings; and there are in the world Arhats who have attained rightly and practiced rightly.

“Those who, having personally realized and attained this world and the world beyond through direct knowledge in this very life, declare: ‘Birth is exhausted for us; the holy life has been lived; what was to be done has been accomplished; we know no further existence beyond this’—this, monks, is that single moment, that single occasion for a person’s dwelling in the holy life.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:
1. Having obtained the human state here in this well-proclaimed True Dharma, those who do not attain the fruit—their opportunity has passed away.
2. Many unfavorable conditions have been declared as obstacles for a person;
yet this [opportunity] which has now appeared before you is extremely difficult to find in the worlds.
The attainment of human birth and the teaching of the true Dharma— one who desires their own welfare must certainly strive to make these two things fruitful.
4. "May we know some of the True Dharma"—let not this moment pass you by;
for those who have let the moment pass grieve when cast into the hells.
5. But having destroyed this certainty of the True Dharma, one will experience birth and death in saṃsāra for a very long time;
scorched by existence for a very long time, like a merchant whose wealth has vanished.
But those who, having attained human status, act according to the words of the Teacher within the well-expounded True Dharma— they penetrate this opportune moment.
The wise who are mindful of the moment and devoted solely to the holy life—
restraint has been taught by the Visionary, the Kinsman of the Sun. Guarded by these [precepts] and possessed of mindfulness, they dwell free from outflows.
"Having severed all latent tendencies along with the arrows of Māra’s army,
those who have attained the destruction of the outflows (āsravakṣaya) have indeed reached the further shore in this world.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
